questions.text:
Tuatara have lived in Aotearoa New Zealand for around 60 million years. The earliest ferns found in New Zealand date back roughly 300 million years.

The timeline below runs from 300 million years ago (earliest ferns) to today, with five arrows labelled 1 to 5 at equal intervals.

Which arrow best shows 60 million years ago on this timeline?
questions.markingGuide: The 5 arrows divide the timeline into 6 equal sections of 50 million years each. Arrow 1 = 250 mya, Arrow 2 = 200 mya, Arrow 3 = 150 mya, Arrow 4 = 100 mya, Arrow 5 = 50 mya. 60 mya is closest to Arrow 5 (50 mya). Accept 5.

questions.text:
A kereru (wood pigeon) weighs 650 grams. It eats a large karaka berry that weighs 13 grams.

How many times heavier is the kereru than the berry?
questions.markingGuide: 650 / 13 = 50. The kereru is 50 times heavier than the berry.

questions.text:
A pair of tui birds nests once or twice each year. Each nest produces 2 to 4 chicks.

If a pair of tui nests every year and all chicks survive, about how many chicks would you expect from one pair in 6 years? Show the calculations you used to get your answer.
questions.markingGuide: This is an estimation question — accept any reasonable answer between 12 and 48 with clear working. Common correct approaches: (1) 1 nest × 3 chicks (mid of 2–4) × 6 years = 18. (2) Minimum: 1 × 2 × 6 = 12. (3) Maximum: 2 × 4 × 6 = 48. (4) Mid-range nests: 1.5 × 3 × 6 = 27. Student must show their working — nests per year × chicks per nest × number of years.

questions.text:
In 2010, a conservation group planted native trees on a reserve. The graph below shows how many trees were alive each year.

Calculate the average number of new trees added per year between 2012 and 2018.
questions.markingGuide: From the graph: 2012 ≈ 35 trees, 2018 ≈ 175 trees. Increase = 175 - 35 = 140 trees over 6 years. Average per year = 140 ÷ 6 ≈ 23.3 trees. Accept any answer between 22 and 25.

questions.text:
Volunteers measured the heights of 25 young kauri trees at a nursery. The histogram below shows the distribution of tree heights. The median height was 1.4 m.

Does the data suggest some of these trees were recently planted? Explain your answer using information from the histogram.
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — some trees are quite short (0.6–1.0 m), which suggests they were planted more recently
questions.markingGuide: Student must say yes AND refer to specific heights from the data. Trees below about 1.2 m are likely more recently planted since established nursery kauri are typically 1.2–2.0 m. Accept reference to heights below the median or in the 0.6–1.0 m range as evidence of younger plantings.

questions.text:
A nature reserve is located about 150 km south of Hamilton.

Using the information that the reserve is approximately 150 km away, and knowing that Hamilton is in the central North Island, which of these towns is closest to where the reserve might be?

(A) Tauranga (about 105 km east of Hamilton)
(B) Taupō (about 150 km south of Hamilton)
(C) New Plymouth (about 200 km south-west of Hamilton)
(D) Rotorua (about 110 km south-east of Hamilton)
(E) Whanganui (about 260 km south-west of Hamilton)
questions.markingGuide: Student must identify the correct letter. Taupō is approximately 150 km south of Hamilton. Accept B.

questions.text:
Wiremu creates a growing triangle pattern using toothpicks.

Pattern 1 uses 3 toothpicks, Pattern 2 uses 9 toothpicks, Pattern 3 uses 19 toothpicks, Pattern 4 uses 33 toothpicks.

The differences between consecutive patterns are: 6, 10, 14 (increasing by 4 each time).

How many toothpicks would Pattern 5 need, in total?
questions.markingGuide: The pattern of total toothpicks is: 3, 9, 19, 33, ... The differences are: 6, 10, 14, ... (increasing by 4 each time). So the next difference is 18. 33 + 18 = 51 toothpicks for Pattern 5.

questions.text:
Hana is designing a woven mat pattern. The mat has six numbered horizontal stripes (1–6) running through the design.

The pattern repeats every 3 stripes. Lines of reflection symmetry pass through stripes 2 and 5.

Which numbers show lines of reflection symmetry in Hana's design? There is more than one answer.
questions.markingGuide: Lines of reflection symmetry in the woven mat pass through stripes 2 and 5 (the horizontal lines of symmetry that divide each repeating section). Accept 2 and 5 only.

questions.text:
Standard proportions for a cartoon character show the head is 1/4 of the total figure height, and the legs start at 1/2 of the total height. A student's drawing has the legs starting at 2/5 of the total height.

Is the leg position correct? Use fractions to explain your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: No — the legs should start at 1/2 but they start at 2/5, which is too high up
questions.markingGuide: Student must compare fractions: 1/2 = 0.5 and 2/5 = 0.4. Since 2/5 < 1/2, the legs start too high up (the upper body is too short). Accept any response that correctly compares these fractions and reaches a justified conclusion.

questions.text:
A trophy has the shape of a rectangular base with a triangular top (like a house shape). When viewed from the front, you see the full rectangle and triangle. When viewed from the right side, you see a rectangle only (no triangle visible).

Which of these shapes shows the correct top view of the trophy?

(A) A circle
(B) A rectangle
(C) A triangle
(D) A hexagon
(E) An L-shape
questions.markingGuide: Looking from above, the trophy with a rectangular base and triangular roof would appear as a rectangle (the footprint of the base). Accept B.

questions.text:
In 1990, a rare NZ coin sold for $400. In 2024, the same coin sold for $2 million.

How many $400 coins could you buy for $2 million?

Tick the correct answer.

The drive from Auckland to Rotorua takes three hours and 42 minutes.

How much time is that rounded to the nearest hour?
questions.markingGuide: 3 hours 42 minutes. 42 minutes is more than 30 minutes, so it rounds up to 4 hours.

questions.text:
A large fish tank holds 15 litres of water when full and weighs 15.372 kilograms.

How much does the empty fish tank weigh, in grams?

Note: One litre of water weighs one kilogram.
questions.markingGuide: 15 litres of water weighs 15 kg. Total weight is 15.372 kg. Empty tank = 15.372 - 15 = 0.372 kg = 372 grams.

questions.text:
Each of five bottles holds 1.5 litres of cordial.

How many 250 mL cups can you fill from all five bottles?
questions.markingGuide: Total cordial = 5 x 1.5 L = 7.5 L = 7500 mL. Number of cups = 7500 / 250 = 30.

questions.text:
Water makes up about 55% of an adult dog's body weight and about 75% of a puppy's body weight. This puppy weighs 4 kilograms, while the adult dog weighs 8 kilograms.

How much more water, in kilograms, does the adult dog have in their body than the puppy has in their body?
questions.markingGuide: Puppy water: 75% of 4 kg = 3 kg. Adult dog water: 55% of 8 kg = 4.4 kg. Difference: 4.4 - 3 = 1.4 kg.

questions.text:
Here is Tama's internet bill for one month.

FibreLine: Data used 240 GB, Rate $/GB = ?, Charge $72.00.

How much does Tama pay per gigabyte (GB) of data?

Note: $/GB means dollars per gigabyte.

Mere's whanau want to save water. There are four people in Mere's whanau.

Mere has two ideas for saving water:
• Reducing daily shower time from 8 minutes to 4 minutes per person.
• Running the washing machine once every two days rather than every day.

Use the table below to work out which of Mere's two ideas would save the most water. Explain your answer using information from the table.
questions.expectedAnswer: Reducing shower time saves more water
questions.markingGuide: Student must compare both ideas using table data. Idea 1 (shower time): Saving per person = 80 - 40 = 40 litres/day. For 4 people = 160 litres/day. Idea 2 (washing machine): Running every 2 days saves 120/2 = 60 litres/day. Shower reduction (160 L) saves more than washing machine (60 L). Accept answer with correct calculations shown.

questions.text:
The chart below shows the average sunshine hours for each month of the year in Dunedin.

Calculate the average monthly sunshine hours across the three summer months (Dec, Jan, Feb).
questions.markingGuide: From the chart: Dec = 185, Jan = 190, Feb = 165. Sum = 185 + 190 + 165 = 540. Average = 540 / 3 = 180 hours. Accept 180.

questions.text:
Pasifika Festival is a cultural event held every year in Auckland. The chart below shows approximate attendance figures.

(There was no event in 2020 or 2021 due to COVID-19.)

About how many more people attended Pasifika Festival in 2022 than in 2015?
questions.markingGuide: From the data: 2022 attendance = 65,000, 2015 attendance = 25,000. Difference = 65,000 - 25,000 = 40,000. Accept 40,000.

questions.text:
Pasifika Festival organisers think attendance will reach 85,000 by 2026.

Using the attendance data from the chart above, do you agree or disagree? Explain your answer using the data.
questions.expectedAnswer: Agree — attendance has been increasing steadily and 85,000 follows the trend
questions.markingGuide: Student should reference specific data. Agree: attendance has been growing by about 5,000–10,000 each year, so 85,000 by 2026 is reasonable. Disagree: growth may slow down; there was no data for 2020–2021. Accept either position if supported by evidence from the data.

questions.text:
Here are the ticket prices for a school cultural showcase:

Ticket options:
• $6.00 — Standard (online, fixed night)
• $8.00 — Flexi (online, any night)
• $10.00 — Door entry on the night

If you buy Standard tickets online for two nights, you get a 25% discount off the total.

Three adults want to attend on both Friday and Saturday.

What will the total cost be for the group?
questions.markingGuide: 3 adults, Standard online ($6.00), 2 nights each. Total before discount: 3 x $6.00 x 2 = $36.00. 25% discount: $36.00 x 0.25 = $9.00. Total: $36.00 - $9.00 = $27.00.

questions.text:
A school fun run has 12 competing teams from different zones. The pie chart below shows how many teams come from each zone.

Each team has the same chance of winning. What is the probability that a team from the East zone wins?

Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.markingGuide: Count East teams: 2 out of 12 total. Probability = 2/12 = 1/6. Accept 2/12, 1/6, or equivalent.

questions.text:
The timetable below shows the schedule for rugby and netball games at a school sports day.

By the time all the morning rugby games have finished (not counting breaks), how many total minutes of rugby game time have been played?
questions.markingGuide: There are 3 rugby games shown in the timetable (Game 1, Game 2, Game 3), each lasting 25 minutes (9:00-9:25, 9:30-9:55, 10:00-10:25). Total rugby time = 3 × 25 = 75 minutes.

questions.text:
A marching group starts in Formation A: 4 rows of 10 performers with a flag bearer at the front (40 performers plus flag bearer). They then move to Formation B: 5 rows of 8 performers with the flag bearer at the front (still 40 performers plus flag bearer).

What is the smallest number of performers from Formation A that need to change rows to make Formation B?
questions.markingGuide: Formation A has 4 rows of 10 (40 performers). Formation B has 5 rows of 8 (40 performers). Keep 8 performers in each of the original 4 rows (32 stay in place). Move 2 performers out of each of those 4 rows to form the new 5th row: 4 × 2 = 8 performers moved. This creates a 5th row of exactly 8. Minimum number of performers that need to change rows = 8.
